p: Adonizedek king of Jerusalem sent unto: That is, "Lord of justice", so tyrants take for themselves glorious names, when indeed they are the very enemies of God and all justice.
war against it: So envious the wicked are, when any depart from their hand.
Fear them not: Lest Joshua should have thought that God had sent this great power against him for his unlawful league with the Gibeonites, the Lord here strengthens him.
hailstones than they whom the children: So we see that all things serve to execute God's vengeance against the wicked.
Jasher: Some read, the book of the righteous, meaning Moses: the Chaldea text reads, in the book of the Law, but it is likely that it was a book thus named, which is now lost.
fought for Israel: By taking away the enemies hearts and destroying them with the hail stones.
peace: Or in safety, so that none gave them as much as an evil word.
necks of these kings: Signifying what would become of the rest of God's enemies, seeing that kings themselves were not spared.
vale: Some read, Ashedoth, which signifies the descents of the hills.
Gilgal: Where the ark was, there to give thanks for their victories.
